lines.text: PEARL HARBOR, ON THE EVE OF 7 DECEMBER 1941

lines.para: Home of the US Pacific Fleet. Eight battleships are in port, most of them moored in a row along Ford Island. The harbour is shallow, about twelve metres: a torpedo attack there is judged impossible. No net protects the battleships.

On 26 November, six Japanese aircraft carriers left the Kuril Islands in secret, under radio silence. On board, more than 350 aircraft. And torpedoes modified for shallow water: the lesson of Taranto.
Hickam, Wheeler, Kaneohe: the island’s airfields were all in Popov’s questionnaire.
